'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
***[[Battle of Chasiv Yar]]
****[[Russian forces]] take control of the Novy district of [[Chasiv Yar]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], Ukraine. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/russia-ukraine-war-chasiv-yar-dnipro-russian-offensive-territorial-gains/ (CBS News)]
***One person is killed and at least 14 others are injured in [[Russia]]n [[guided bomb]] and missile attacks across [[Kharkiv Oblast]], Ukraine. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-attacks-kharkiv-region-kill-one-injure-four-2024-07-03/ (Reuters)]
**[[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)|Russian strikes against infrastructure]]
***[[Dnipro strikes (2022–present)|Dnipro strikes]]
****At least five people are killed and 53 others are injured when Russian [[Drone warfare|drones]] and [[missile]]s hits [[civilian]] [[infrastructure]] in [[Dnipro]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ce78nr3253jo (BBC News)]
**[[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***[[NATO]] nations agree to grant Ukraine [[Euro|€]]40 billion ([[US$]]43 billion) in [[military aid]] in 2025. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/nato-members-agree-40-billion-euro-financial-pledge-ukraine-diplomats-say-2024-07-03/ (Reuters)]
**[[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant crisis]]
***Three [[Loitering munition|kamikaze drones]] attack an [[electrical substation]] for the Russian-held [[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant]], injuring eight workers, causing forest fires near the plant's switchyard, and leaving [[Enerhodar]] without power or water. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukrainian-drones-injure-zaporizhzhia-nuclear-power-plant-workers-say-russian-2024-07-03/ (Reuters)] [https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-russia-zaporizhzhya-drone-attack-iaea-grossi/33020612.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[:he:פיגוע הדקירה בקניון בכרמיאל|Karmiel mall stabbing attack]]
***An [[Israel]]i soldier is killed and another is injured in a [[stabbing attack]] at a mall in [[Karmiel]], Israel. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/two-people-injured-attack-israeli-mall-police-2024-07-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israeli occupation of the West Bank]]
***The [[Israeli government]] approves the seizure of {{conv|12.7|km2|sqmi}} of [[Palestinian territories|Palestinian]] land in the [[Jordan Valley]], representing the largest land seizure in the [[West Bank]] in more than three decades. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-hamas-war-news-07-03-2024-033deab379a16efdf9989de8d6eaf0f8 (AP)]
*[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**An [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] strike kills Mohammed Nasser, a top commander in [[Hezbollah]], in [[Tyre, Lebanon|Tyre]], [[Lebanon]]. Nasser is one of the highest-ranking Hezbollah members to die in the conflict. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2024/07/03/senior-hezbollah-field-commander-killed-in-israeli-strike-two-security-sources-say (Al Arabiya)]
**Hezbollah launches a barrage of at least 100 [[Katyusha rocket]]s, towards [[northern Israel]], targeting Israeli military positions, in retaliation for the killing of Nasser. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/3/hezbollah-launches-barrage-of-rockets-at-israel-after-top-commander-killed (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Five people, including former [[senator]] [[Hidayat Ullah]], are killed when their vehicle en route to an election rally strikes a [[roadside bomb]] in [[Bajaur District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-former-senator-killed-bombing-northwest-f34c65a421aab752536acb2318aca7fa (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*Scientists announce the discovery of the world's oldest [[cave painting]], depicting three people gathered around a large red pig, estimated to be at least 51,200 years old, in Leang Karampurang cave in the [[Caves in the Maros-Pangkep karst|Maros-Pangkep region]], [[South Sulawesi]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/4/worlds-oldest-artwork-discovered-in-indonesian-cave (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Beryl (2024)|Hurricane Beryl]]
***The death toll from Hurricane Beryl in the eastern [[Caribbean]] increases to nine, with deaths reported in [[Grenada]], [[Saint Vincent and the Grenadines]], and [[Venezuela]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/hurricane-beryl-churns-towards-jamaica-bringing-floods-least-two-reported-killed-2024-07-02/ (Reuters)]
**Four police officers are killed in floods caused by Tropical Storm Chris in [[Tepetlán]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.elimparcial.com/mexico/2024/07/04/mueren-cuatro-policias-arrastrados-por-un-rio-tras-paso-de-la-tormenta-tropical-chris-en-veracruz/ (''El Imparcial'')]
*[[2024 India-Bangladesh floods]]
**At least sixteen people are killed and more than 300,000 others are [[forced displacement|displaced]] by [[flood]]s and [[landslide]]s in [[Assam]] and [[Arunachal Pradesh]], [[India]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/climate-change/news/assam-flood-kaziranga-air-force-rescue-b2572432.html (''The Independent'')]

*Three people are killed and three others are missing after a [[fishing boat]] sinks off the coast of [[Marinha Grande]], [[Portugal]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2024/07/03/shipwreck-off-the-coast-of-portugal-kills-three-three-missing- (Al Arabiya)]
*At least 26,000 people are forced to [[emergency evacuation|evacuate]] amidst dozens of large [[wildfire]]s in [[Northern California]], [[United States]]. [https://www.npr.org/2024/07/03/nx-s1-5028568/northern-california-wildfire-evacuations-heat (NPR)]

'''Health and environment'''
*Temperatures in [[Moscow]], Russia, reach {{conv|32.7|C}}, the highest on this day since 1917. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2024/07/03/summer-heatwave-sweeps-russia-breaking-dozens-of-temperature-records-a85590 (''The Moscow Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-swelters-heat-wave-moscow-breaks-1917-record-early-july-2024-07-04/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Investigators in [[Germany]] and [[Sweden]] arrest eight suspects allied with [[Syrian President]] [[Bashar al-Assad]]'s [[government of Syria|government]] over alleged participation in [[crimes against humanity]] in [[Syria]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20240703-germany-sweden-arrest-eight-over-syria-crimes-against-humanity (France 24)]
*The [[Supreme Court of Japan]] rules that [[Japan|the country]]'s [[Forced sterilization in Japan|forced sterilization law]], which was in effect from 1948 to 1996, was [[Constitution of Japan|unconstitutional]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20240703-japan-s-top-court-rules-forced-sterilisation-law-unconstitutional (France 24)]
*[[Sierra Leone]] outlaws [[child marriage]], setting the [[legal age of marriage]] to 18 years. Offenders could face up to 15 years in prison and/or a fine of around US$4,000, with witnesses to child marriages also facing possible jail or fines. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/sierra-leone-outlaws-child-marriage-witnesses-weddings-can-face-jail-time/ (CBS News)]
*The [[Federal government of the United States|U.S.]] [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|Environmental Protection Agency]] fines [[General Motors]] $145.8 million for [[United States vehicle emission standards|excess emissions]] found in 5.9 million GM vehicles. [https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/gm-pay-1458-million-penalty-after-us-finds-excess-emissions-59-million-vehicles-2024-07-03/ (Reuters)]
